turns.request: We just got the keys to the penthouse on the 12th floor of Sunday Towers in Arabkir and want the whole flat furnished before we move in in November. We are Narek (52) and Lilit (49) Hakobyan. Narek is a commercial lawyer: he often works from home until late, reads contracts on paper, and needs a real office with a big desk, a proper ergonomic chair, closed storage for files and a spot where he can take video calls with a calm background. Lilit is a pastry chef who teaches masterclasses on Saturdays; she is the one who cooks, so the kitchen stays hers, but the table is the heart of this family. Our daughter Mariam (19) studies in Vienna and is home for summers and New Year; her room must stay hers (she paints, needs a desk by the window and space for an easel), and when she is away it is the guest room for Lilit's mother from Gyumri, who is 76 and needs a bed that is easy to get in and out of and a chair with arms. Every Sunday we host lunch for 10 people, sometimes 12 with cousins, and in summer we eat on the big balcony off the living room. So: a dining table for at least 10 in the living room, with the sofa corner separate from it, and a summer table on the balcony for 6. Use the two big bedrooms (about 25 m2 each) for us and for Narek's office, and the smaller one (17 m2) for Mariam. Style: warm and grown-up, walnut and oak, travertine, deep green and rust accents, linen, lots of plants, brass lamps. We hate grey minimalism, glossy white furniture and anything that looks like a hotel. Our bedroom needs a king-size bed, a big wardrobe and blackout curtains (Narek sleeps badly), and a reading chair for Lilit. The entrance should welcome guests: a bench to take off shoes, a coat rack for 12 coats in winter, a mirror. Budget: 16,000,000 AMD for furniture.

record.message: I’ll first check the room sizes and access against your bedroom, office and hosting needs, then build the furnishing scheme around warm woods, green and rust, and comfortable lighting.

record.question: The bedrooms and indoor dining fit, but the living-room balcony’s narrow L-shape and fixed storage prevent comfortable seating for six with clear access; would you prefer?

requests: We just got the keys to the penthouse on the 12th floor of Sunday Towers in Arabkir and want the whole flat furnished before we move in in November. We are Narek (52) and Lilit (49) Hakobyan. Narek is a commercial lawyer: he often works from home until late, reads contracts on paper, and needs a real office with a big desk, a proper ergonomic chair, closed storage for files and a spot where he can take video calls with a calm background. Lilit is a pastry chef who teaches masterclasses on Saturdays; she is the one who cooks, so the kitchen stays hers, but the table is the heart of this family. Our daughter Mariam (19) studies in Vienna and is home for summers and New Year; her room must stay hers (she paints, needs a desk by the window and space for an easel), and when she is away it is the guest room for Lilit's mother from Gyumri, who is 76 and needs a bed that is easy to get in and out of and a chair with arms. Every Sunday we host lunch for 10 people, sometimes 12 with cousins, and in summer we eat on the big balcony off the living room. So: a dining table for at least 10 in the living room, with the sofa corner separate from it, and a summer table on the balcony for 6. Use the two big bedrooms (about 25 m2 each) for us and for Narek's office, and the smaller one (17 m2) for Mariam. Style: warm and grown-up, walnut and oak, travertine, deep green and rust accents, linen, lots of plants, brass lamps. We hate grey minimalism, glossy white furniture and anything that looks like a hotel. Our bedroom needs a king-size bed, a big wardrobe and blackout curtains (Narek sleeps badly), and a reading chair for Lilit. The entrance should welcome guests: a bench to take off shoes, a coat rack for 12 coats in winter, a mirror. Budget: 16,000,000 AMD for furniture.
A: four seats on that balcony, keeping larger meals in the living room
